ACL 2022Text generation · Human evaluation

How Do Seq2Seq Models Perform on End-to-End Data-to-Text Generation?

Xunjian Yin, Xiaojun Wan

Peking University

Paper ↗Code ↗ACL Anthology ↗

A high generation score does not explain what a model gets wrong. Fine-grained human annotation reveals how copying, pre-training, and dataset structure affect data-to-text errors.

Result
ToTTo human error scores: adding a copy mechanism to Transformer cuts Omission from 19.74 to 7.48 but raises Addition from 4.38 to 11.01 (lower is better).
New vs prior
Ferreira et al. (2019) compare pipeline and end-to-end data-to-text systems, and PolyTope (Huang et al., 2020) annotates summarization errors; this work applies MQM error annotation to five Seq2Seq models on four datasets.
Limitation
Each model–dataset score rests on 80 annotated outputs, and only models up to 220M parameters were tested; T5-large and BART-large were omitted for compute reasons.
01 / The research question

Fluent text can put the right entity in the wrong role

In the paper's Table 2 example, the input gives Round Rock as the largest city of Williamson County and Georgetown as its county seat; the output calls Georgetown the largest city and omits the county seat. The sentence reads naturally, yet it contains a distorted fact and a missing one, each needing a different repair, and a single overlap score cannot say which.

Earlier human evaluations of data-to-text systems covered few samples, datasets, models, or error dimensions. Here annotators locate every error and record its type and severity, giving each model an error profile instead of one number.

Closest prior work

Ferreira et al. (2019) compared pipeline and end-to-end architectures for neural data-to-text generation, and Thomson and Reiter (2020) proposed a protocol for human evaluation of accuracy. Most model comparisons still rely on BLEU or ROUGE, which can disagree with human judgment (Novikova et al., 2017a; Reiter, 2018), and existing human evaluations cover few samples, datasets, models, or error dimensions. This study adapts the MQM-based PolyTope scheme of Huang et al. (2020), developed for summarization, to annotate five Seq2Seq models on four data-to-text datasets.

02 / Inside the method

Faithfulness and content selection are distinct requirements

The study adapts the Multidimensional Quality Metrics (MQM) framework, via the PolyTope scheme for summarization, to eight error types. Inaccuracy Intrinsic distorts information in the input; Inaccuracy Extrinsic adds information absent from it; Addition, narrower than hallucination, is unnecessary material taken from the input. Omission, Positive-Negative Aspect, Duplication, Word Form, and Word Order complete the set. Addition versus Omission matters most for ToTTo, where only highlighted cells should be described.

Published example · Table 2

Annotate the output, then compare with the paper

The study scores outputs from human error annotations: each error segment receives a type and a severity, the severity weight is multiplied by the segment length, and the total is normalized by the word count (Section 4.3). Each error span gets a type and a severity: minor, major, or critical. Five annotators, selected from eight by a qualification test, labeled 1,600 outputs (80 inputs × four datasets × five models), each twice; outputs whose two error scores diverged too much were replaced, and annotators did not know which model produced an output.

  1. 01

    Compare representative models

    Evaluate Transformer, a pointer-generator Transformer, T5-small, T5-base, and BART-base on E2E, WebNLG, WikiBio, and ToTTo.

  2. 02

    Annotate specific errors

    Use an adapted MQM framework with eight error types covering accuracy and fluency, rather than relying only on automatic scores.

  3. 03

    Analyze the contributing factors

    Compare error profiles across architectures, pre-training, model sizes, and dataset structures to identify useful techniques and remaining weaknesses.

03 / Reading the evidence

An architectural improvement can move errors between categories

  • 19.74 → 7.48

    ToTTo Omission score with copying

    Adding a copy mechanism to Transformer cuts the severity-weighted Omission score but raises Addition from 4.38 to 11.01 (Table 5; lower is better).

  • 62.88 vs 59.96

    E2E BLEU, T5-small vs T5-base

    BLEU ranks T5-small above T5-base, while human MQM scores reverse the order, 86.04 versus 96.36 (Tables 3–4).

Measured · Table 6 printed averages. Shaded rows are the two error types of the Table 2 example (Omission and Inaccuracy Intrinsic); they carry the two largest average penalties. The other six types together sum to 5.37.

Copying preserves input content but also pulls in content the description does not need: on ToTTo, the copy model's Omission score falls by more than half while its Addition score more than doubles (Table 5). The paper attributes the extra additions to an auto-regressive decoder that copies long input spans and is hard to interrupt.

BLEU's overall trend agrees with human evaluation, but the paper reports a Pearson correlation of 0.61 between BLEU and the accuracy score and only 0.08 for fluency (Section 6), and rankings of close models can flip, as on E2E. Pre-training has the largest effect in Table 3: pre-trained models beat the others by a wide margin on every dataset except E2E.

Scope. All four datasets are English and differ in how much content selection they require, from fully specified WebNLG triples and partially specified E2E records to ToTTo's highlighted cells and WikiBio's unspecified infobox content (Table 1). Read the study ↗

Read the abstract

With the rapid development of deep learning, Seq2Seq paradigm has become prevalent for end-to-end data-to-text generation, and the BLEU scores have been increasing in recent years. However, it is widely recognized that there is still a gap between the quality of the texts generated by models and the texts written by human. In order to better understand the ability of Seq2Seq models, evaluate their performance and analyze the results, we choose to use Multidimensional Quality Metric(MQM) to evaluate several representative Seq2Seq models on end-to-end data-to-text generation. We annotate the outputs of five models on four datasets with eight error types and find that 1) copy mechanism is helpful for the improvement in Omission and Inaccuracy Extrinsic errors but it increases other types of errors such as Addition; 2) pre-training techniques are highly effective, and pre-training strategy and model size are very significant; 3) the structure of the dataset also influences the model’s performance greatly; 4) some specific types of errors are generally challenging for seq2seq models.
